precepts.text: And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. Now we understand the context of love in the Bible: walking after God's commandments.
precepts.point: The acknowledgment of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ: that goes back to the chapter before.
precepts.why:
Some of you may be new, so understand what “knit together in love” means. It is not talking about rubbing each other's back. It is not talking about putting lotion on each other's feet. John defines it: “And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it.”

Now we understand the context of love in the Bible: walking after God's commandments. That is the love that knits us together as one man, the same love as being kindly affectioned one to another and in honour preferring one another.

So read Colossians again with that understanding: “That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ”. Our hearts are knit together when we keep God's commandments together, and that brings us to the riches of the full assurance of understanding and the mystery of God, which goes back to the chapter before.

precepts.text: And this is love, that we walk after his commandments; it never changed from old covenant to new.
precepts.point: Do not just say you love God, put action behind it. Sisters, come out of the pants and mini skirts and put on a modest dress, and be in subjection to your own husbands; brothers, put on your fringes, stop dyeing your hair, and marry the mother of your children instead of leaving her a baby mama. When you will not do what he told you to do, no words out of your mouth can make you love him; your actions show you actually hate him.

note.label: Deuteronomy 10: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

precepts.why:
“And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it.” Moses asks what the Lord requires, and it all boils down to keeping the commandments of the Lord and his statutes. John says the same: love is walking after his commandments. It never changed from old covenant to new; it is “as ye have heard from the beginning”.

Here is your purpose in life, the stipulations for the body the Most High gave you, and what you must do to please him as the children of Israel: love him and serve him with all thy heart and with all thy soul by keeping his commandments, which he commands thee for thy good. That is how you love and serve God until the day we return to the dust or he sends his son to redeem us from the land of our captivity. Loving God is not something you say; it is a walk.
